verses.1:1: Now it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus, the same Ahasuerus who reigned from India to Cush over one hundred and twenty-seven provinces,
verses.1:2: in those days when King Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom, which was in Shushan the citadel,
verses.1:3: in the third year of his reign he made a feast for all his princes and his servants; the army of Persia and Media, the nobles, and the princes of the provinces were before him,
verses.1:4: as he displayed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the honor of his splendid majesty for many days, one hundred and eighty days.
verses.1:5: And when these days were fulfilled, the king made a feast of seven days for all the people who were present in Shushan the citadel, from the greatest to the least, in the court of the garden of the king's palace.
verses.1:6: There were white and blue cotton hangings, fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings and pillars of marble; couches of gold and silver were upon a mosaic pavement of porphyry, marble, mother-of-pearl, and dark stone.
verses.1:7: And drinks were served in vessels of gold, the vessels differing one from another, and royal wine was in abundance, according to the bounty of the king.
verses.1:8: And the drinking was according to the law: there was no compulsion, for so the king had directed all the officers of his house, that they should do according to each man's pleasure.
verses.1:9: Queen Vashti also made a feast for the women in the royal house that belonged to King Ahasuerus.
verses.1:10: On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seven eunuchs who ministered in the presence of King Ahasuerus,
verses.1:11: to bring Queen Vashti before the king wearing the royal crown, in order to show the peoples and the princes her beauty, for she was lovely to behold.
verses.1:12: But Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command delivered by the hand of the eunuchs; therefore the king became exceedingly angry, and his fury burned within him.
verses.1:13: Then the king spoke to the wise men who understood the times, for such was the king's custom before all who knew law and justice;
verses.1:14: and those closest to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media who saw the king's face and sat foremost in the kingdom:
verses.1:15: "According to the law, what shall be done to Queen Vashti, because she has not carried out the command of King Ahasuerus delivered by the hand of the eunuchs?"
verses.1:16: And Memucan answered before the king and the princes, "Queen Vashti has not wronged the king alone, but also all the princes and all the peoples who are in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus.
verses.1:17: For the queen's deed will go forth to all the women, causing them to despise their husbands in their eyes when they say, 'King Ahasuerus commanded Queen Vashti to be brought before him, yet she did not come.'
verses.1:18: And this very day the noble ladies of Persia and Media who have heard of the queen's deed will speak of it to all the king's princes, and there will be plenty of contempt and wrath.
verses.1:19: If it pleases the king, let a royal decree go forth from before him, and let it be written among the laws of Persia and Media so that it may not be altered, that Vashti shall come no more before King Ahasuerus; and let the king give her royal position to another who is better than she.
verses.1:20: And when the king's edict which he shall make is heard throughout all his kingdom—great though it is—all the women will give honor to their husbands, from the greatest to the least."
verses.1:21: And the saying pleased the king and the princes, and the king did according to the word of Memucan.
verses.1:22: So he sent letters to all the king's provinces, to every province according to its script and to every people according to its language, that every man should be master in his own house and speak in the language of his own people.
verses.2:1: After these things, when the wrath of King Ahasuerus had subsided, he remembered Vashti, and what she had done, and what had been decreed against her.
verses.2:2: Then the king's young men who ministered to him said, "Let fair young virgins be sought for the king.
verses.2:3: And let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather every fair young virgin to Shushan the citadel, to the house of the women, into the custody of Hegai the king's eunuch, keeper of the women; and let their beauty treatments be given them.
verses.2:4: Then let the maiden who pleases the king reign as queen in place of Vashti." And the thing pleased the king, and he did so.
verses.2:5: Now there was a certain Jew in Shushan the citadel whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite,
verses.2:6: who had been carried away into exile from Jerusalem with the captives who had been taken into exile with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away.
verses.2:7: And he had brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle's daughter, for she had neither father nor mother. The maiden was lovely in form and fair of countenance; and when her father and mother died, Mordecai took her as his own daughter.
verses.2:8: So it came to pass, when the king's command and his decree were heard, and when many maidens were gathered to Shushan the citadel into the custody of Hegai, that Esther was taken to the king's palace, into the custody of Hegai, keeper of the women.
verses.2:9: Now the maiden pleased him, and she won his favor; so he hastened to provide her with her beauty treatments and her portions, and with the seven choice maidservants appointed to be given her from the king's palace; and he moved her and her maidservants to the best place in the house of the women.
verses.2:10: Esther had not disclosed her people or her kindred, for Mordecai had charged her that she should not disclose it.
verses.2:11: And every single day Mordecai walked to and fro before the court of the house of the women, to learn of Esther's welfare and what was being done with her.
verses.2:12: Now when each maiden's turn arrived to go in to King Ahasuerus, after she had been twelve months according to the regulation for the women—for so were the days of their beautification fulfilled: six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with spices and the beauty treatments of the women—
verses.2:13: in this manner the maiden would go in to the king: whatever she asked for was given her to go with her from the house of the women to the king's palace.
verses.2:14: In the evening she would go in, and in the morning she would return to the second house of the women, to the custody of Shaashgaz the king's eunuch, keeper of the concubines. She would not go in to the king again unless the king delighted in her and she was summoned by name.
verses.2:15: Now when the turn came for Esther—the daughter of Abihail, the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her as his daughter—to go in to the king, she requested nothing except what Hegai the king's eunuch, keeper of the women, advised. And Esther won favor in the sight of all who beheld her.
verses.2:16: So Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus, to his royal palace, in the tenth month, which is the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
verses.2:17: And the king loved Esther more than all the other women, and she found grace and favor in his sight more than all the virgins; so he set the royal crown upon her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.
verses.2:18: Then the king made a great feast for all his princes and his servants, the Feast of Esther; and he proclaimed a holiday for the provinces and gave gifts according to the bounty of the king.
verses.2:19: And when virgins were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate.
verses.2:20: Now Esther had still not disclosed her kindred or her people, just as Mordecai had charged her; for Esther obeyed the command of Mordecai just as when she was brought up by him.
verses.2:21: In those days, while Mordecai sat at the king's gate, two of the king's eunuchs, Bigthan and Teresh, keepers of the threshold, became furious and sought to lay hands on King Ahasuerus.
verses.2:22: And the matter became known to Mordecai, who told it to Queen Esther; and Esther reported it to the king in Mordecai's name.
verses.2:23: And when the matter was investigated and found to be true, both of them were hanged upon a gallows; and it was written in the book of the chronicles in the presence of the king.
verses.3:1: After these things King Ahasuerus promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and exalted him, and set his seat above all the princes who were with him.
verses.3:2: And all the king's servants who were at the king's gate bowed down and paid homage to Haman, for so the king had commanded concerning him. Yet Mordecai would neither bow down nor pay homage.
verses.3:3: Then the king's servants who were at the king's gate said to Mordecai, "Why do you transgress the king's commandment?"
verses.3:4: Now it came to pass, when they spoke to him day after day and he would not listen to them, that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai's words would stand; for he had told them that he was a Jew.
verses.3:5: And when Haman saw that Mordecai neither bowed down nor paid homage to him, Haman was filled with wrath.
verses.3:6: Yet he disdained to lay hands on Mordecai alone, for they had told him of the people of Mordecai; therefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the entire kingdom of Ahasuerus, the people of Mordecai.
verses.3:7: In the first month, which is the month of Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, they cast Pur—that is, the lot—before Haman from day to day and from month to month, to the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar.
verses.3:8: Then Haman said to King Ahasuerus, "There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the peoples in all the provinces of your kingdom; and their laws differ from those of every other people, and they do not keep the king's laws. Therefore it is not to the king's profit to let them remain.
verses.3:9: If it pleases the king, let a decree be written that they be destroyed, and I will weigh out ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those who carry out the business, to bring it into the king's treasuries."
verses.3:10: So the king took his signet ring off his hand and gave it to Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.
verses.3:11: And the king said to Haman, "The silver is given to you, and the people also, to do with them as seems good in your eyes."
verses.3:12: Then the king's scribes were summoned on the thirteenth day of the first month, and everything was written according to all that Haman commanded to the king's satraps, and to the governors who were over every province, and to the princes of every people, to every province according to its script and to every people according to its language. In the name of King Ahasuerus it was written, and it was sealed with the king's signet ring.
verses.3:13: And letters were sent by the hand of couriers to all the king's provinces, to destroy, to slay, and to annihilate all the Jews, both young and old, little children and women, in one day, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar, and to plunder their spoil.
verses.3:14: A copy of the writing was to be issued as a decree in every province and published openly to all the peoples, that they should be ready for that day.
verses.3:15: The couriers went forth in haste at the king's command, and the decree was issued in Shushan the citadel. And the king and Haman sat down to drink, while the city of Shushan was in perplexity.
verses.4:1: Now Mordecai learned all that had been done, and Mordecai tore his garments and put on sackcloth and ashes; and he went out into the midst of the city and cried out with a great and bitter cry.
verses.4:2: He went as far as the front of the king's gate, for no one might enter the king's gate clothed in sackcloth.
verses.4:3: And in every province, wherever the king's command and his decree arrived, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping, and lamentation; sackcloth and ashes were spread as a bed for many.
verses.4:4: Then Esther's maidens and her eunuchs came and told her, and the queen was deeply distressed; and she sent garments to clothe Mordecai and to remove his sackcloth from him, but he would not accept them.
verses.4:5: So Esther summoned Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs whom he had appointed to attend her, and gave him a charge to Mordecai, to learn what this was and why it was.
verses.4:7: And Mordecai told him all that had befallen him, and the exact sum of silver that Haman had promised to weigh out into the king's treasuries for the Jews, to destroy them.
verses.4:8: He also gave him a copy of the written decree that had been issued in Shushan for their annihilation, to show Esther and explain to her, and to charge her to go in to the king to make supplication to him and to plead before him on behalf of her people.
verses.4:9: So Hathach came and reported to Esther the words of Mordecai.
verses.4:10: Then Esther spoke to Hathach and sent him back with a charge to Mordecai:
verses.4:11: "All the servants of the king and the people of the king's provinces know that for any man or woman who enters the inner court to the king without being summoned, there is but one law—to be put to death—except the one to whom the king holds out the golden scepter, that he may live. Yet as for me, I have not been summoned to come to the king these thirty days."
verses.4:12: So they reported Esther's words to Mordecai.
verses.4:13: Then Mordecai told them to reply to Esther: "Do not suppose within yourself that in the king's house you will escape any more than all the other Jews.
verses.4:14: For if you remain wholly silent at this time, respite and deliverance will arise for the Jews from another quarter, while you and your father's house shall perish. And who knows whether it is for a time such as this that you have attained to royalty?"
verses.4:15: Then Esther told them to reply to Mordecai:
verses.4:16: "Go, assemble all the Jews who are found in Shushan, and fast on my behalf; do not eat and do not drink for three days, night or day. I and my maidens also will fast in like manner. Then I will go in to the king, though it is contrary to the law; and if I perish, I perish."
verses.4:17: So Mordecai departed and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.
verses.5:1: Now it came to pass on the third day that Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner court of the king's palace, facing the king's house, while the king was sitting upon his royal throne in the royal house, facing the entrance of the house.
verses.5:2: And it came to pass, when the king saw Queen Esther standing in the court, that she obtained favor in his sight; and the king extended to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand. Then Esther drew near and touched the tip of the scepter.
verses.5:3: Then the king said to her, "What is your wish, Queen Esther? And what is your request? Up to half the kingdom, it shall be granted to you."
verses.5:4: And Esther answered, "If it pleases the king, let the king and Haman come today to the banquet that I have prepared for him."
verses.5:5: Then the king said, "Fetch Haman quickly, to fulfill the word of Esther." So the king and Haman came to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
verses.5:6: At the banquet of wine the king said to Esther, "What is your petition? It shall be given to you. And what is your request? Even to half the kingdom, it shall be performed."
verses.5:7: Then Esther answered and said, "My petition and my request is this:
verses.5:8: If I have found favor in the sight of the king, and if it pleases the king to grant my petition and perform my request, let the king and Haman come to the banquet which I shall prepare for them, and tomorrow I will do according to the king's word."
verses.5:9: So Haman went out that day joyful and glad of heart; yet when Haman saw Mordecai at the king's gate, and that he neither rose nor stirred before him, Haman was filled with wrath against Mordecai.
verses.5:10: Nevertheless Haman restrained himself and went to his house; and he sent and brought his friends and his wife Zeresh.
verses.5:11: Then Haman recounted to them the splendor of his riches, the multitude of his sons, and all the ways in which the king had magnified him and how he had exalted him above the princes and servants of the king.
verses.5:12: Moreover Haman said, "Even Queen Esther brought no one with the king to the banquet she prepared except myself; and tomorrow also I am invited by her together with the king.
verses.5:13: Yet all of this avails me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate."
verses.5:14: Then his wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, "Let a gallows be made, fifty cubits high, and in the morning speak to the king that Mordecai may be hanged upon it; then go joyfully with the king to the banquet." And the counsel pleased Haman, so he had the gallows made.
verses.6:1: That night sleep fled from the king; so he commanded to bring the book of the records of the chronicles, and they were read before the king.
verses.6:2: And it was found written that Mordecai had reported concerning Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs, keepers of the threshold, who had sought to lay hands on King Ahasuerus.
verses.6:3: Then the king asked, "What honor and dignity have been bestowed on Mordecai for this?" And the king's attendants who ministered to him answered, "Nothing has been done for him."
verses.6:4: And the king asked, "Who is in the court?" Now Haman had come into the outer court of the king's house to speak to the king concerning hanging Mordecai on the gallows which he had prepared for him.
verses.6:5: The king's attendants said to him, "Behold, Haman is standing in the court." And the king said, "Let him come in."
verses.6:6: So Haman came in, and the king said to him, "What shall be done for the man whom the king delights to honor?" Now Haman said in his heart, "Whom would the king delight to honor more than myself?"
verses.6:7: And Haman answered the king, "For the man whom the king delights to honor,
verses.6:8: let them bring a royal robe which the king has worn, and a horse on which the king has ridden and on whose head a royal crown has been set.
verses.6:9: And let the robe and the horse be delivered into the hand of one of the king's most noble princes, that they may array the man whom the king delights to honor, and lead him on horseback through the city square, and proclaim before him, 'Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!'"
verses.6:10: Then the king said to Haman, "Hasten, take the robe and the horse, just as you have spoken, and do so for Mordecai the Jew who sits at the king's gate! Leave nothing undone of all that you have spoken."
verses.6:11: So Haman took the robe and the horse, arrayed Mordecai, and led him on horseback through the city square, and proclaimed before him, "Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!"
verses.6:12: Afterward Mordecai returned to the king's gate, while Haman hurried to his house, mourning and with his head covered.
verses.6:13: When Haman recounted to his wife Zeresh and all his friends everything that had befallen him, his wise men and his wife Zeresh said to him, "If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, is of the seed of the Jews, you shall not prevail against him, but shall surely fall before him."
verses.6:14: While they were still speaking with him, the king's eunuchs arrived and hastened to bring Haman to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
verses.7:1: So the king and Haman came to drink with Esther the queen.
verses.7:2: And on the second day also, at the banquet of wine, the king said to Esther, "What is your petition, Queen Esther? It shall be granted to you. And what is your request? Up to half of the kingdom, it shall be done."
verses.7:3: Then Queen Esther answered and said, "If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it pleases the king, let my life be granted to me as my petition, and my people as my request.
verses.7:4: For we have been sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to be annihilated. If we had been sold as male servants and female servants, I would have kept silent, although the adversary could not compensate for the loss to the king."
verses.7:5: Then King Ahasuerus spoke and said to Queen Esther, "Who is he, and where is he, whose heart has emboldened him to do such a thing?"
verses.7:6: And Esther said, "An adversary and an enemy—this wicked Haman!" And Haman was struck with terror before the king and the queen.
verses.7:7: Then the king arose in his wrath from the banquet of wine and went into the palace garden, while Haman stayed behind to plead for his life from Queen Esther, for he saw that evil was determined against him by the king.
verses.7:8: When the king returned from the palace garden to the hall of the banquet of wine, Haman had fallen upon the couch where Esther was. Then the king said, "Will he even assault the queen with me in the house?" As the word went out from the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.
verses.7:9: Now Harbona, one of the eunuchs before the king, said, "Behold, also, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman made for Mordecai, who spoke good on behalf of the king, is standing at the house of Haman." And the king said, "Hang him upon it!"
verses.7:10: So they hanged Haman upon the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the wrath of the king subsided.
verses.8:1: On that day King Ahasuerus gave to Queen Esther the house of Haman, the adversary of the Jews. And Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had declared what he was to her.
verses.8:2: And the king took off his signet ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai; and Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.
verses.8:3: Now Esther spoke again before the king, fell at his feet, and wept and implored him to put away the evil of Haman the Agagite and his scheme which he had devised against the Jews.
verses.8:4: And the king held out the golden scepter toward Esther. So Esther arose and stood before the king.
verses.8:5: And she said, "If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor before him, and the matter is right before the king, and I am pleasing in his sight, let it be written to revoke the letters, the scheme of Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to annihilate the Jews who are in all the provinces of the king.
verses.8:6: For how can I bear to see the calamity that will overtake my people? And how can I bear to see the destruction of my kindred?"
verses.8:7: Then King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther and to Mordecai the Jew, "Behold, I have given the house of Haman to Esther, and they have hanged him upon the gallows because he stretched out his hand against the Jews.
verses.8:8: Now you yourselves write concerning the Jews as is good in your eyes, in the king's name, and seal it with the king's signet ring; for a writing that is written in the king's name and sealed with the king's signet ring cannot be revoked."
verses.8:9: So the king's scribes were summoned at that time, in the third month, which is the month of Sivan, on the twenty-third day of the month; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded to the Jews, and to the satraps, the governors, and the princes of the provinces from India to Cush, one hundred and twenty-seven provinces, to every province according to its own script, to every people according to its own language, and to the Jews according to their own script and according to their own language.
verses.8:10: And he wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, sealed it with the king's signet ring, and sent letters by couriers on horseback, riding swift royal steeds bred from the royal stud.
verses.8:11: By these letters the king granted to the Jews who were in every city to assemble and defend their lives, to destroy, to slay, and to annihilate every armed force of any people or province that might assault them, both little ones and women, and to plunder their spoil,
verses.8:12: on one day in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar.
verses.8:13: A copy of the document was to be issued as a decree in every province and openly published to all the peoples, that the Jews might be ready on that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.
verses.8:14: The couriers, riding the swift royal steeds, went out, hastened and pressed on by the king's command; and the decree was issued in Shushan the citadel.
verses.8:15: And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, with a great crown of gold and a mantle of fine linen and purple; and the city of Shushan shouted aloud and rejoiced.
verses.8:16: For the Jews there was light and gladness, joy and honor.
verses.8:17: And in every province and in every city, wherever the king's word and his decree arrived, there was gladness and joy for the Jews, a feast and a festive day. And many among the peoples of the land declared themselves Jews, for the dread of the Jews had fallen upon them.
verses.9:1: Now in the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar, on the thirteenth day of the month, when the king's command and his decree came due to be executed, on the day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to have mastery over them, the very opposite came to pass, that the Jews themselves gained mastery over those who hated them.
verses.9:2: The Jews gathered together in their cities throughout all the provinces of King Ahasuerus to lay hands on those who sought their harm; and no one could stand before them, for the dread of them had fallen upon all the peoples.
verses.9:3: And all the princes of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and those who did the king's work supported the Jews, because the dread of Mordecai had fallen upon them.
verses.9:4: For Mordecai was great in the king's house, and his fame went out throughout all the provinces; for this man Mordecai grew greater and greater.
verses.9:6: And in Shushan the citadel the Jews slew and destroyed five hundred men.
verses.9:7: And Parshandatha, and Dalphon, and Aspatha,
verses.9:8: and Poratha, and Adalia, and Aridatha,
verses.9:9: and Parmashta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Vaizatha—
verses.9:10: the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the adversary of the Jews, they slew; yet on the plunder they did not lay their hand.
verses.9:11: On that day the number of those who were slain in Shushan the citadel came before the king.
verses.9:12: And the king said to Queen Esther, "In Shushan the citadel the Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men and the ten sons of Haman. What have they done in the rest of the king's provinces? Now what is your petition? It shall be granted to you. And what is your further request? It shall be done."
verses.9:13: Then Esther said, "If it pleases the king, let it be granted to the Jews who are in Shushan to act tomorrow also according to today's decree, and let the ten sons of Haman be hanged upon the gallows."
verses.9:14: So the king commanded this to be done; a decree was issued in Shushan, and they hanged the ten sons of Haman.
verses.9:15: And the Jews who were in Shushan assembled also on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and slew three hundred men in Shushan; yet on the plunder they did not lay their hand.
verses.9:16: Now the rest of the Jews who were in the king's provinces assembled and defended their lives, had rest from their enemies, and slew seventy-five thousand of those who hated them; yet on the plunder they did not lay their hand.
verses.9:17: This took place on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar; and on the fourteenth day of the month they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
verses.9:18: But the Jews who were in Shushan assembled on the thirteenth day and on the fourteenth day of the month; and on the fifteenth day of the month they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
verses.9:19: Therefore the Jews of the villages, who dwell in the unwalled towns, observe the fourteenth day of the month of Adar as a day of gladness and feasting, a festive day, and for sending portions to one another.
verses.9:20: And Mordecai wrote down these things and sent letters to all the Jews who were in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, both near and far,
verses.9:21: to establish among them that they should observe the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and the fifteenth day of the same, year by year,
verses.9:22: as the days on which the Jews gained rest from their enemies, and as the month that was turned for them from sorrow into gladness and from mourning into a festive day, that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, of sending portions to one another and gifts to the poor.
verses.9:23: So the Jews accepted what they had begun to do and what Mordecai had written to them.
verses.9:24: For Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the adversary of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that is, the lot, to crush them and to annihilate them;
verses.9:25: but when it came before the king, he commanded by letter that his wicked scheme, which he had devised against the Jews, should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged upon the gallows.
verses.9:26: Therefore they called these days Purim, after the name of Pur. Therefore, because of all the words of this letter, and what they had seen concerning this matter, and what had come upon them,
verses.9:27: the Jews established and took upon themselves, and upon their descendants, and upon all who joined themselves to them, without fail, that they should observe these two days according to what was written concerning them and at their appointed time, year by year;
verses.9:28: and that these days should be remembered and observed throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city, and that these days of Purim should never cease from among the Jews, nor should the remembrance of them come to an end among their descendants.
verses.9:29: Then Queen Esther, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter concerning Purim.
verses.9:31: To confirm these days of Purim at their appointed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had established for them, and as they had established for themselves and for their descendants regarding the matters of the fasts and their lamentation.
verses.9:32: And the decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim, and it was written in the book.
verses.10:1: And King Ahasuerus levied a tribute upon the land and the coastlands of the sea.
verses.10:2: And all the deeds of his authority and his might, and the full account of the greatness of Mordecai, to which the king exalted him, are they not recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
verses.10:3: For Mordecai the Jew was second in rank to King Ahasuerus, great among the Jews and favored by the multitude of his brethren, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all his descendants.

notes.1:1: Cush refers to ancient Nubia and Upper Ethiopia south of Egypt; the pairing of India and Cush marks the eastern and southwestern limits of the Persian Empire under Ahasuerus (Xerxes I).
notes.1:6: This description uses rare loanwords for fine white cotton (karpas) and four luxury paving materials—porphyry, white marble, mother-of-pearl, and dark stone—whose exact mineral identifications remain partly uncertain.
notes.1:16: Ketiv/Qere: the written consonantal text (ketiv) spells the prince's name Mwmkn, while the traditional reading (qere) reads Memucan, matching verses 14 and 21.
notes.2:3: The Hebrew text spells this official's name Hege here and Hegai in verses 8 and 15; it is rendered Hegai consistently.
notes.2:18: The Hebrew term hanachah literally denotes a "granting of rest" and may refer either to a public holiday or to a royal remission of taxes and tribute.
notes.2:23: Gallows renders Hebrew ets, literally "tree" or "wooden pole," reflecting the Persian practice of public hanging or impalement on a stake.
notes.3:4: Ketiv/Qere: the written text (ketiv) reads "in their speaking" (with the preposition be-), while the traditional reading (qere) reads "when they spoke" (with the preposition ke-).
notes.3:7: Pur is a loanword from Akkadian puru meaning "lot," which the narrator glosses with the Hebrew term haggoral ("the lot") and which later gives the Festival of Purim its name.
notes.3:12: Satraps translates an Old Persian loanword (achashdarpenim) designating the chief royal viceroys who oversaw major regions of the empire.
notes.4:4: The written text (ketiv) spells the verb with an extra vowel letter, while the read form (qere) preserves the standard feminine plural form meaning "and they came."
notes.4:7: The written text (ketiv) uses a double-yod spelling for the gentilic plural, while the read form (qere) gives the standard plural form "for the Jews."
notes.4:14: "Another quarter" translates Hebrew "another place," long recognized as a discreet allusion to divine providence in a book that never explicitly mentions the name of God.
notes.5:1: "Put on her royal robes" translates a concise Hebrew expression literally meaning "put on royalty," referring to royal apparel.
notes.5:14: "Gallows" renders the Hebrew word for "wood" or "tree," denoting in Persian usage a lofty wooden stake or pole for public impalement or hanging, fifty cubits (roughly seventy-five feet) tall.
notes.6:1: "Sleep fled from the king" renders a vivid Hebrew idiom literally meaning "the king's sleep wandered away."
notes.6:8: In the Hebrew syntax, "on whose head a royal crown has been set" modifies the horse, reflecting the ancient Persian custom of adorning the king's steed with a royal crest or diadem.
notes.6:13: "Shall surely fall" reflects the emphatic Hebrew infinitive absolute construction, stressing the certainty of Haman's downfall.
notes.7:4: The closing Hebrew clause literally reads 'for the adversary [or: affliction] is not equal to the loss of the king,' indicating either that the adversary could not offset the royal loss or that the hardship of servitude would not warrant troubling the king.
notes.7:9: The Hebrew word translated 'gallows' literally means 'tree' or 'wooden pole,' referring to a tall stake for public hanging or impalement, fifty cubits (about seventy-five feet) high.
notes.8:1: Here and in 8:7, 8:13, 9:15, and 9:18, the ketiv preserves an extended double-yod spelling while the qere reads the standard form for 'the Jews.'
notes.8:10: The Persian loanword 'achashteranim' denotes horses reserved for royal service, paired with 'benei harammakhim,' referring to thoroughbred stock from the royal stud.
notes.8:13: The ketiv reads 'atudim' and the qere reads the standard Hebrew form 'atidim,' both meaning 'ready' or 'prepared.'
notes.8:17: The reflexive verb 'mityahadim' denotes 'declaring themselves Jews' or 'identifying as Jews,' encompassing religious conversion or protective alignment with the Jewish community.
notes.9:19: The ketiv reads 'happeruzim' and the qere reads 'happerazim,' referring to rural Jews living in unwalled villages as distinct from those inside the fortified city of Shushan.
notes.9:25: The Hebrew feminine suffix translated 'when it came' can refer either to Haman's plot coming to the king's attention or to Queen Esther coming before the king.
notes.9:27: The ketiv uses the singular verb 'veqibbel' ('and took,' treating 'the Jews' as a collective as in 9:23), whereas the qere reads the plural 'veqibbelu' to match the preceding plural verb 'established.'
notes.10:1: The consonantal text writes Ahasuerus defectively without the letter vav, while the traditional reading supplies the standard spelling Ahasuerus. Hebrew mas denotes royal tribute or taxation levied across the mainland and the maritime islands or coastlands.
notes.10:2: The phrase full account renders Hebrew parashah, meaning a detailed statement or exact record, and chronicles renders divrei hayyamim, literally the matters of the days, referring to the official royal annals of Media and Persia.
notes.10:3: Hebrew zera, literally seed, denotes Mordecai's posterity and by extension the whole lineage of his people, while shalom encompasses both peace and enduring well-being.
